matters.title: ADOPT A RESOLUTION TO APPROVE FINDINGS AND AWARD A CONTRACT TO TROJAN TECHNOLOGIES FOR REPLACEMENT PARTS, ON-CALL REPAIR AND MAINTENANCE SERVICES
matters.text:
...title
ADOPT A RESOLUTION TO APPROVE FINDINGS AND AWARD A CONTRACT TO TROJAN TECHNOLOGIES FOR REPLACEMENT PARTS, ON-CALL REPAIR AND MAINTENANCE SERVICES

..recommended action
RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the City Council adopt a resolution to:

1. Approve findings pursuant to Stockton Municipal Code section 3.68.070 in support of an exception to the competitive bidding process. 

2. Authorize a five-year contract with Trojan Technologies of London, Ontario, Canada, not-to-exceed $1,250,000, for materials as well as on-call repair and maintenance services (Exhibit 1 to the Resolution).

It is further recommended that the City Manager be authorized to take appropriate and necessary actions to carry out the purpose and intent of this resolution.

...body
Summary

The Municipal Utilities Department (MUD) includes the Water, Wastewater, and Stormwater utilities that are supported by user fees and regulated for the protection of public health and the environment. The Wastewater Utility operates the Regional Wastewater Control Facility (RWCF), an advanced tertiary treatment plant with a 55 million gallons per day (MGD) capacity located next to the San Joaquin River.

MUD staff operate and maintain equipment used in wastewater treatment including an ultraviolet (UV) system used in the wastewater disinfection process. The UV system requires routine maintenance and repair to effectively disinfect wastewater.

If approved by the City Council, this action will authorize a five-year contract with Trojan Technologies of London, ON, Canada, not-to-exceed $1,250,000, for materials, on-call repair, and maintenance services.

DISCUSSION

Background

The City of Stockton Regional Wastewater Control Facility Modifications Project construction changed the sewer treatment to an activated sludge process and replaced equipment and processes that were 40 to 70 years old and beyond their useful life. During construction, the project team installed a Trojan Technologies UV system, UVSIGNA, as part of the tertiary wastewater disinfection process. The UVSIGNA system is a proprietary brand that requires Trojan Technologies replacement parts and certified services to maintain proper operation.  
 
Present Situation

The UVSIGNA system is routinely monitored by MUD Maintenance staff and requires frequent maintenance, parts, and repairs to continue performing as designed by the manufacturer. Currently, Trojan Technologies is the sole available source for parts and certified service. 

If approved by the City Council, this action will authorize a five-year contract with Trojan Technologies for a not-to-exceed amount of $1,250,000. The proposed contract includes the materials and services necessary to maintain the system in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications.

Findings

According to the Stockton Municipal Code (SMC) section 3.68.070, the City Council may approve findings which support and justify an exception to the competitive bidding process. The following findings support and justify and exception:

1. Trojan Technologies is the only source for replacement parts and repair services in the United States. 

2. Routine maintenance, replacement parts, and repairs are standard practice required to preserve the UVSIGNA system's ability to effectively disinfect wastewater during the treatment process.

3. The UVSIGNA system requires the use of original manufacturer components and services for proper operation, performance guarantees, and lowest life-cycle cost.

4. Maintaining and repairing the UVSIGNA system is more cost-effective than replacing it with an alternative UV system. Accordingly, the proposed contract serves the public's best interest. 

FINANCIAL SUMMARY

There are sufficient funds in the Wastewater Maintenance Division accounts 6512-000-630013-610-000-00-65-000-000 and 6512-000-650001-610-000-00-65-000-00 to pay for parts, repair and maintenance services for FY 2025-26. Funding for the remaining contract term will be budgeted in the same accounts and presented to the City Council for approval during the annual budget process.

This action has no impact on the General Fund or any other unrestricted funds.

matters.title: APPROVE FINDINGS AND AUTHORIZE THE SOLE SOURCE PURCHASE OF GE ORBIT 900 MHZ RADIOS FROM APPLIED TECHNOLOGY GROUP, INC. FOR THE MUNICIPAL UTILITIES DEPARTMENT (CITYWIDE)
matters.text:
..title 
APPROVE FINDINGS AND AUTHORIZE THE SOLE SOURCE PURCHASE OF GE ORBIT 900 MHZ RADIOS FROM APPLIED TECHNOLOGY GROUP, INC. FOR THE MUNICIPAL UTILITIES DEPARTMENT (CITYWIDE)

..recommendation
RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the City Council adopt a resolution to:

Approve findings pursuant to Stockton Municipal Code Section 3.68.070 in support of an exception to the competitive bidding process.

Authorize the purchase of 110 GE Orbit 900 MHz radios from Applied Technology Group, Inc. of Bakersfield, CA, for $317,000.

Authorize the appropriations of Storm, Water, and Wastewater Utility funds in the amount of $317,000 from Fund Balance.

It is also recommended that the City Manager be authorized to take appropriate and necessary actions to carry out the purpose and intent of this resolution.

..body
Summary

The Municipal Utilities Department (MUD) operates and maintains a 900 MHz telemetry radio system that supports communication between remote water, sanitary sewer, and stormwater pump stations, and the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system located at the Regional Wastewater Control Facility (RWCF). The MUD SCADA system gathers real time data from these remote locations to control equipment, monitor site conditions, and inform operations and maintenance staff of issues.

Modernizing the telemetry radio system is essential because the existing radios are more than 20 years old, increasingly unreliable, and difficult to support due to the limited availability of replacement parts. Updating the system will help ensure continued, stable communication for critical water, wastewater, and stormwater operations.

If approved by the City Council, this action will approve findings of an exception to the competitive bidding process and authorize the purchase of 110 GE Orbit 900 MHz radios from Applied Technology Group, Inc. of Bakersfield, CA, for $317,000.




DISCUSSION

Background

MUD’s telemetry radio system delivers vital real-time information to the SCADA system operated at the RWCF. It supports data transmission from 10 groundwater well sites, 28 sanitary sewer pump stations and 75 storm water pump stations. The information provided to SCADA informs operations and maintenance staff of pump status, wet well levels, pump run hours, discharge flow rates, and critical alarms such as pump failures, facility intrusions and high-level conditions.

The current telemetry radio system is more than 20 years old and relies on outdated technology that is increasingly difficult to maintain. Federal guidance from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Department of Homeland Security (DHS), and the American Water Works Association (AWWA) encourages water and wastewater utilities to modernize remote telemetry and SCADA communication systems to ensure reliable operations. Updating these radios aligns with federal recommendations and represents a critical step in improving MUD’s overall system reliability.

Present Situation

The current radio network infrastructure has been past its endoflife for several years, creating significant operational risks. When a radio fails, replacement and repair are increasingly difficult because these older GE units are no longer readily available.

The proposed solution offers a costeffective approach to improving MUD’s cybersecurity defenses and safeguarding essential services. After a thorough review of modern product options, staff recommend purchasing GE Orbit radios from Applied Technology Group, Inc., of Bakersfield, CA, for $317,000. These new radios are compatible in form, fit, and function with the existing equipment, ensuring a smooth transition while enhancing system resilience.

Applied Technology Group, Inc. is a technology company that offers full-service radio/wireless communications and related services for public safety, commercial industries, education, private enterprise, and government agencies. They specialize in SCADA products and are the only authorized vendor of GE Orbit 900 MHz radios in this region.

Findings

Stockton Municipal Code Section 3.68.070(A)(4) provides an exception to the competitive bidding requirements when the City Council approves findings that support and justify the purchase through a sole source vendor.

Proposed findings to support this purchase are:

The purchase of GE Orbit 900 MHz radios is necessary because they are compatible in form, fit, and function with the existing infrastructure, which uses proprietary protocols.

Replacing the currently in place end-of-life equipment is essential to maintaining a reliable radio system for monitoring and controlling the water, sanitary sewer, and stormwater systems that provide vital public health services to the Stockton community.

Applied Technology Group, Inc., is the only authorized vendor of GE Orbit 900 MHz radios in this region.

Purchasing the GE Orbit 900 MHz radios from Applied Technology Group, Inc. will allow MUD to avoid additional costs associated with replacing auxiliary components, as the new radios use the same cabling, antennas, mounts, power supplies, and related hardware.

FINANCIAL SUMMARY

With this action, $317,000 will be appropriated from MUD Wastewater, Water, and Stormwater Utility Fund Balance for the replacement of the aging radios.

matters.title: ADOPT A RESOLUTION TO AUTHORIZE A THREE-YEAR SOLE SOURCE AGREEMENT WITH INSOURCE SOFTWARE SOLUTIONS, INC. FOR AVEVA SOFTWARE SUBSCRIPTION, MAINTENANCE, AND SUPPORT SERVICES FOR THE MUNICIPAL UTILITIES DEPARTMENT (ALL DISTRICTS - CITYWIDE)
matters.text:
..title
ADOPT A RESOLUTION TO AUTHORIZE A THREE-YEAR SOLE SOURCE AGREEMENT WITH INSOURCE SOFTWARE SOLUTIONS, INC. FOR AVEVA SOFTWARE SUBSCRIPTION, MAINTENANCE, AND SUPPORT SERVICES FOR THE MUNICIPAL UTILITIES DEPARTMENT (ALL DISTRICTS – CITYWIDE)

..recommended action
RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the City Council adopt a resolution to:

Approve findings pursuant to Stockton Municipal Code Section 3.68.070(A)(4) supporting an exception to the competitive bidding process for InSource Software Solutions, Inc. as the sole source vendor for AVEVA software subscription, maintenance, and support services.

Authorize the City Manager, or designee, to execute a three-year agreement with InSource Software Solutions, Inc. for AVEVA software subscription, maintenance, and support services in an amount not to exceed $180,000.00.

It is also recommended that the City Manager be authorized to take appropriate and necessary actions to carry out the purpose and intent of this resolution.

..body
Summary

The Municipal Utilities Department (MUD) uses AVEVA software as a critical component of the City’s Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system. The software supports monitoring, control, automation, alarming, historical data collection, and reporting for critical utility operations, including the Delta Water Treatment Plant, the Regional Wastewater Control Facility, water distribution sites, sanitary sewer pump stations, and storm water pump stations.  Every MUD facility equipped with SCADA uses AVEVA software.

The current AVEVA software subscription, maintenance, and support services must be renewed to maintain access to software updates, maintenance releases, technical support, compatibility support, and vendor support for the existing SCADA environment. These services are necessary to help ensure the continued reliability and functionality of MUD’s utility control and monitoring systems.

If approved by the City Council, this action will approve findings of an exception to the competitive bidding process and authorize the City Manager to execute a three-year sole source agreement and/or purchase orders with InSource Software Solutions Inc., the sole provider of AVEVA software subscription, maintenance, and support services.



DISCUSSION

Background

For more than 25 years MUD utilized Wonderware software to operate and monitor critical water, wastewater, storm water, and pumping facilities. In or around 2018, Wonderware was rebranded as AVEVA. Following that transition, the City purchased its AVEVA subscription annually through AVEVA Select California. In 2025, InSource Solutions, Inc. purchased AVEVA Select California, making InSource Software Solutions, Inc. the sole provider of AVEVA (formerly Wonderware) software in our region.

The AVEVA software is necessary to operate the City Municipal Utilities Department’s Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems. These systems gather real-time data to control equipment, monitor site conditions, generate alarms, record selected historical data, and provide operational and regulatory reporting for wastewater treatment, stormwater pump stations, and water distribution networks. 

To use AVEVA, the City must maintain an active subscription that includes maintenance and support services. These services provide essential access to software updates, maintenance releases, licensing assistance, technical support, and compatibility updates for server operating systems and related infrastructure.

Present Situation

The proposed three-year renewal will provide continued AVEVA Flex subscription and Customer FIRST Premium Support services from October 2026 through October 2029.

InSource Software Solutions, Inc. is the only authorized distributor for California and is authorized to sell AVEVA software licenses, renew AVEVA Customer First support contracts, and provide authorized technical training. Because AVEVA is the SCADA software currently implemented by MUD, other SCADA software vendors cannot provide software updates, maintenance releases, licensing support, or technical support for the City’s existing AVEVA platform.

InSource Software Solutions, Inc. provided the City with a total cost of $179,180 for the City’s AVEVA software subscriptions. Staff recommend approval of a not-to-exceed amount of $180,000.00 to account for the quoted subscription renewals.

Findings

Pursuant to the Stockton Municipal Code (SMC) section 3.68.070, the City Council may approve findings that support and justify an exception to the competitive bidding process. The following findings support and justify an exception:

AVEVA software subscription, maintenance, and support services are required to maintain the City’s existing SCADA software environment used by MUD to monitor and control critical utility infrastructure.

The requested subscription and support services are proprietary to the AVEVA software platform and must be obtained through an authorized AVEVA distributor.

InSource Software Solutions, Inc. is the sole authorized AVEVA distributor for California and is authorized to sell AVEVA software licenses, renew AVEVA Customer First support contracts, and provide authorized technical training.

Other SCADA software vendors cannot provide updates, maintenance releases, licensing support, or technical support for the City’s existing AVEVA software platform.

Replacing the existing SCADA software platform would require significant cost, staff time, programming, testing, training, and operational disruption with no practical benefit for the purpose of renewing existing software maintenance and support.

Failure to renew these services would leave critical software unsupported, increasing cybersecurity and reliability risks. Over time, this could affect SCADA performance, slow troubleshooting, and heighten the risk of outages across treatment plants, pump stations, distribution facilities, and reporting systems.

FINANCIAL SUMMARY

If approved by the City Council, this action will authorize a three-year agreement and/or purchase orders with InSource Software Solutions, Inc. for AVEVA software subscription, maintenance, and support services in an amount not to exceed $180,000.00. The quoted three-year subscription renewal cost is $179,180.00.
